Zero Conditional
You use Zero Conditional when you talk about real or possible situations.

When you use the Zero Conditional, you have to keep in mind that both clauses (if clause + main clause) are in simple present form. It's important to take into account that you use zero conditional to express a result that always happens.

Use the following rule to make a sentence using zero conditional:

If/When + Simple present + ,(comma) + Simple present.

Example:
- If the company has too many databases, implement a data warehouse.

Note that you can change the order of the clauses without changing the idea. 

- Implement a data warehouse if the company has too many databases.
Plus, I need to get a high score if I want to pass this subject because I have a lot of bad grades.
In addition, this architecture can use a virtual approach to data warehouses if the volume of data to analyze is huge.
Conjuctions: And, As, Because , But
You use conjunctions when you want to connect words, phrases, clauses, or sentences.

Remember that a conjunction is a part of the speech, and it is divided into two groups:

Coordinating Conjunctions can join two different clauses to create a compound sentence. This type of conjunctions gives an equal emphasis to two clauses. In this case, we work on two coordinating conjunctions which are : And – But

You use And when you want to link or add one clause to another one.
Example:
  • Data warehousing has different architectures, and it's really important to differentiate them.

    You use But when you want to show contrast between to clauses. Example:
  • Data warehousing uses some architectures, but it doesn't have data storage on them.

    Note: It's important to use a comma (,) before some coordinating conjunctions when you have two independent clauses.

    Subordinating Conjunctions can join clauses, but in this case, one clause becomes dependent upon the other one. Subordinating conjunctions permit to do the necessary transition between one clause to another. In this case, we work on two subordinating conjunctions which are BECAUSE – AS

    You use     Because and As when you want to refer to the cause or reason for the previous sentence.

    Example:
  • Data extraction is really important because you can get crucial information from different databases.
  • The single-layer architecture avoids data redundancies, as it minimizes the amount of data stored.
Moreover, this architecture is very functional, as it creates a common reference data for a whole enterprise.

Data Warehouse Architecture Layer
Data warehouse architecture commonly has two classifications.

<span class =”italic”>It's really important to keep in mind the function of the two classifications of the data warehouse architecture. The first one which gathers three types of layers (single-layer architecture, two layer architecture, and three layer architecture) is structure-oriented, and it depends on the amount of layers that the architecture uses. On the other hand, the second classification is determined by the way, in which different layers are used to create enterprise-oriented or department-oriented views of data warehouses.

Steve: Hi, Nick! You look so stressed, what are you doing?
Nicky: Hi, Steve! I'm studying for tomorrow's exam, but there are some topics that I don't understand. Plus, I need to get a high score if I want to pass this subject because I have a lot of bad grades.
Steve: Which topics don't you get?
Nicky: Basically, it's just data warehouse architecture.

Steve: I studied that topic last semester. So, I can help you if you want.
Nicky: Of course!
Steve: Good! To start, keep in mind some important properties that are crucial for a data warehouse system like separation, scalability, extensibility, security, and administerability. Do you have the function of each one clear?
Nicky: Yes, I know them perfectly. However, I think that my trouble is the three types of layer architecture.

Steve: Don't worry! Firstly, the single-layer architecture permits to minimize the quantity of data the company stores, so it removes data redundancies. In addition, this architecture can use a virtual approach to data warehouses if the volume of data to analyze is huge. However, the failure of this architecture is the separation between analytical and transactional processing. Is it clear?
Nicky: Sure!
Steve: Okay! Secondly, the goal of the two-layer architecture is to separate physical available sources and data warehouses. Also, it brings different benefits to data warehouses such as quality information, specific design solutions, and reliability, among others. Finally, the three-layer architecture allows materializing the operational data left after cleansing and integrating the source data. Moreover, this architecture is very functional, as it creates a common reference data for a whole enterprise, and it separates the problems of source data extraction from problems of data warehouse population.
Nicky: Wow! That was hard, but I understand. I appreciate your help.
Steve: You're welcome, Nicky.
